cases.title: Youxiao Road resettlement, Guiyang
cases.point: Approximate. A point about halfway along the 7.04 km Youxiao Road, which runs from Youzhajie in central Guiyang to Xiaozhai in the Longdongbao area. The same loan also paid for rural roads and rural bus terminals spread across the rural districts of Guiyang Municipality; the completion report records 11 segments of rural road, 15 rural bus terminals and one freight depot as built.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Guiyang Transport Project, P093963. Loan IBRD-48810 (L4881-CN) of US$100 million, approved 8 January 2008, signed 18 March 2008, effective 9 June 2008. The closing date was moved from 31 December 2012 to 31 December 2013, and the loan was fully disbursed at US$100 million. The completion report gives the actual total project cost as US$360.7 million against US$314.42 million estimated before appraisal.

cases.conditions: The Independent Evaluation Group's validation records that the loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12), because the project involved land acquisition, housing demolition and household relocation, and its policy on indigenous peoples (OP 4.20), because the project could affect Miao and Buyi minority communities. A Resettlement Action Plan and an Indigenous Peoples Development Plan were written and published before the loan was approved. A restructuring approved in December 2012 added a legal covenant to the loan so that the Bank could keep monitoring resettlement activities until they were finished.

companies.name: Guiyang Municipal Government
companies.role: Executing agency; its Guiyang Project Management Office ran the project day to day

companies.name: Tongyuan Road Construction Development Co. Ltd
companies.role: Implementation agency for the first batch of rural roads and bus terminals until March 2012, when the project office took over the second batch

cases.community: The completion report records 142 households displaced by construction of the Youxiao Road. On the Bank's project launch mission in July 2008 the Bank found that compensation rates being paid for the Youxiao Road resettlement were lower than the rates set in the Resettlement Action Plan. The report says the problem was quickly remedied and that by October 2008 the rates were higher than the plan required. Later Bank missions found resettlement behind schedule on both the road and the rural roads. All 142 households displaced by the Youxiao Road signed contracts for resettlement or compensation only by September 2013, three months before the loan closed; the road itself had opened to traffic on 5 February 2010. The report states that full resettlement would not be completed until December 2014. Land acquisition and resettlement on the Youxiao Road cost US$72.95 million against US$22.07 million estimated at appraisal; on the rural transport component it cost US$33.03 million against US$27.62 million. A Bank mission in September 2009 found about half the first batch of rural roads and bus terminals behind schedule, mainly because of unresolved resettlement issues. Land acquisition and resettlement for two of those roads, the Xiaohegou to Shuikou road and the Weicheng to Liuji road, were finished only one month before the loan closed.
cases.outcome: The completion report rated the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, quality at entry Moderately Unsatisfactory and implementing agency performance Moderately Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group also rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, rated quality at entry Moderately Satisfactory, and raised the risk to the development outcome from Moderate to Significant. It recorded that the Bank had reached an agreement with the Guiyang Municipal Government that monitoring of the remaining safeguards work would carry on under the supervision of a later loan, the Guiyang Rural Roads Project, approved by the Board in March 2014. Six external social monitoring reports were sent to the Bank during implementation, the last in April 2014. No figure appears in either report for how many of the 142 households had been fully resettled by any date.
cases.displaced_label: households displaced by Youxiao Road construction (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 20,850 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. The Bank's completion report gives 142 households displaced by construction of the Youxiao Road and does not give a total number of people for the project as a whole. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation separates people who lost housing from people who only lost land or income.

cases.title: Guiyang-Guangzhou Railway land acquisition and supplemental income programmes
cases.place: Guiyang-Guangzhou railway corridor, Guizhou, Guangxi and Guangdong, China
cases.point: Approximate. A point on the corridor at Yangshuo County, Guilin, Guangxi, one of the nine Guangxi counties and districts listed in the Bank's completion report. The line itself is a new two-track electrified railway of about 857 km running from Guiyang to Guangzhou, and the final alignment crossed 226 villages in 87 townships of 26 counties in three provinces.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Guiyang Guangzhou Railway Project, P107559. Loan IBRD-76780 (L7678-CN) of US$300 million, approved 16 April 2009, effective 26 August 2009, with US$299.49 million disbursed. The closing date was extended by one year, from 31 December 2015 to 31 December 2016, to allow the supplemental income programmes tied to land acquisition to be carried out. The borrower's own contribution came to US$12,755.49 million against US$12,226.56 million estimated.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A and triggered four Bank safeguard policies besides environmental assessment: natural habitats (OP 4.04), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11), involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and indigenous peoples (OP 4.10). A Resettlement Action Plan and an Ethnic Minority Development Plan were written and published before approval. When the line was changed in a restructuring of 2 August 2013 from a mixed freight and passenger railway to a passenger-dedicated line at 250 km/h, the resettlement plan was rewritten for the new alignment and three Supplemental Income Programmes were added, one for each province. Local governments were to carry them out by 2014 and be reimbursed by China Railway Corporation, the GuiGuang company and the three provinces.

companies.name: China Railway Corporation
companies.role: Implementing agency; successor to the Ministry of Railways, which endorsed the resettlement plan at appraisal

companies.name: GuiGuang Railway Company Limited
companies.role: Project company created during implementation; the railway's assets were transferred to it, and it monitored resettlement and processed compensation payments

cases.community: The completion report records that permanently acquired land along the railway affected 26,696 families, 64,030 people, and that temporary land acquisition affected a further 21,643 households, 81,324 people. Elsewhere the same report says more than 60,000 farmers were affected and around 8,000 people were relocated. The Independent Evaluation Group's validation records the appraisal expectations: 32,617 mu of land to be permanently acquired including 18,776 mu of cultivated land, a further 24,078 mu occupied temporarily, about 23,983 households (100,190 persons) affected, seven schools and some infrastructure to be moved, and approximately 1,600 ethnic minority households to be relocated. The three supplemental income programmes were a multiple livelihood fund scheme in Guizhou, a project-related social security programme in Guangxi, and reserved land or fees in Guangdong requiring that 10 per cent of the area acquired be used for the production and development of affected villages. The local governments were to carry them out by 2014. The line was operating from December 2014. The completion report states that the programmes account for about three per cent of total support to project-affected people and that about half of that had not been disbursed when the loan closed. The closing date had already been extended by a year at the end of 2015 because the three programmes had not been completed, and by the end of 2016 they still had not been. An agreement between China Railway Corporation and the three provinces signed on 23 September 2016 transferred CNY 337 million to the provincial implementing agencies. The report's Annex 9, based on a report by an independent consultant hired by China Railway Corporation and current to May 2017, records that in Guangxi RMB 90.46 million of social security funds for nine counties and districts (Sanjiang County in Liuzhou; Longsheng, Lingui, Lingchuan, Yangshuo and Gongcheng counties in Guilin; Zhongshan County, Pinggui District and Babu District in Hezhou) reached municipal authorities on 12 December 2016 and county finance bureau social security accounts between 20 January and 29 March 2017, that the funds were to reach the counties' fiscal and social security accounts by the end of 2017, and that the government was still establishing accounts for the affected farmers. In Guangdong the reserved-land money for six counties and districts in Zhaoqing and Foshan had reached county and district land and resources bureaux and was expected to be paid to villages by the end of May 2017. In Guizhou the county land and resources bureaux received the multi-channel compensation funds in November 2016, and the report states the Guizhou programme was expected to be completed by March 2018. The main text of the same completion report states that only the Guangxi programme was completed by the time the report was prepared, and gives its completion as March 2017. Both statements are in the one report, both are current to May 2017, and the report does not reconcile them.
cases.outcome: The completion report rated the project outcome Highly Satisfactory and the implementation progress rating at loan closing Moderately Satisfactory, the latter because the supplemental income programmes had not been completed. The Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Satisfactory. It rated government and implementing agency performance Satisfactory, and recorded that the implementing agency had completed the land acquisition and paid compensation but that the programmes of two of the three provinces were unfinished at closure. The Bank and the government agreed that the Bank would go on monitoring the programmes after the loan closed, and China Railway Corporation and the GuiGuang company agreed to hire an external monitoring agent to report on progress.
cases.displaced_label: people in 26,696 families whose land was permanently acquired; around 8,000 people were relocated from their homes (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 99,595 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. The Bank's completion report separates the categories: 26,696 families, 64,030 people, lost land permanently; 21,643 households, 81,324 people, were affected by temporary land occupation; and around 8,000 people were relocated from their homes. The appraisal document, as quoted by the Independent Evaluation Group, had expected about 23,983 households, 100,190 persons, to be affected, of whom 63,164 through land acquisition and 3,259 through house demolition.

cases.title: Liupanshui-Zhanyi railway resettlement, Guizhou and Yunnan
cases.place: Liupanshui, Guizhou to Zhanyi, Qujing, Yunnan, China
cases.point: Approximate. A point about halfway along the Liupanshui to Zhanyi railway, which runs from Liupanshui in western Guizhou to Zhanyi in Qujing, Yunnan. The section inside the Kunming Railway Administration is described in the borrower's report as close to 100 km long.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Third National Railway Project, P086515. Loan IBRD-48470 (L4847-CN) of US$200 million, approved 23 January 2007, effective 16 May 2007, with US$199.76 million disbursed. The closing date was moved from 30 June 2012 to 30 June 2013. Total financing required came to RMB 13,285 million against RMB 9,433 million at appraisal.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A and triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP 4.01), natural habitats (OP 4.04) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). The cost of resettlement was normally split half and half between the railway and the provincial governments, and the Ministry of Railways had no mandate to administer resettlement itself; the provincial and local governments did that work. The Bank appraised the project in September 2005 but the loan was not negotiated until November 2006, because the Ministry of Railways needed that time to reach agreement with the Guizhou and Yunnan governments on who would fund the resettlement action plan and how it would be carried out. The completion report describes both as among China's poorest provinces, with limited money and little experience of such plans.

companies.name: Ministry of Railways, Foreign Capital and Technical Import Center
companies.role: Implementing agency; handled relations with foreign lenders

companies.name: Kunming Railway Bureau
companies.role: Railway administration for the Yunnan section; ran land acquisition and demolition there with county governments

companies.name: Chengdu Railway Bureau
companies.role: Railway administration for the Guizhou section

cases.community: The completion report states that delays in funding land acquisition and completing the resettlement of project-affected people held up the start of construction by six months in the Yunnan section and sixteen months in the Guizhou section. It describes two stages to the problem: first the Ministry of Railways and the provincial governments reaching agreement on land compensation rates, then identifying the affected people and compensating or resettling them. The delays arose from disputes between the railway and local governments over the release by the two provinces of their share of the resettlement funding, and then over the level of payments per affected household. The report states that cash compensation for land acquisition in Yunnan Province was paid to affected persons at rates set by local government before July 2009 which were at times below the rates in the resettlement action plan, and that additional spending of RMB 49.7 million by local government and the Ministry of Railways went into drinking water, irrigation, transport and infrastructure in the resettlement villages, with the external monitoring showing that each village's in-kind expenditure was enough to offset its land compensation shortfall. In and around Liupanshui the new tracks were laid in densely populated areas, and resettlement took longer there than elsewhere on the line because suitable urban land had to be acquired before replacement housing could be built; this delayed completion of the Liupanshui hub. The total completed land acquisition cost came to RMB 1.02 billion, 104 per cent more than the estimate in the resettlement plan, because both the amount of demolition and the compensation rates rose. Sixteen per cent less land was finally acquired than planned after the alignment was changed, while the number of houses demolished rose by 16 per cent. Eight concentrated resettlement sites were built. Households losing housing could take either a right to exchange property or cash. The borrower's own section of the report states that on the roughly 100 km Liupanshui to Zhanyi second line inside the Kunming Railway Administration, 431,886 square metres of housing were demolished and 5,587.4 mu of land newly acquired; that average compensation along the whole line was RMB 24,000 per mu for land and RMB 500 per square metre for houses, of which the railway owner paid RMB 13,000 per mu and RMB 240 per square metre and local government subsidised the rest; that 3,702 mu of temporary land was used, with RMB 17.24 million paid in rent, RMB 9.67 million in compensation for 671 mu that could not be reclaimed and RMB 7.31 million for crops and fruit trees; and that by completion all compensation had been distributed and everyone whose land or house was taken had been resettled in place.
cases.suppression: The borrower's own section of the completion report states that land requisition and demolition were not to be carried out by force against unwilling residents, and that from the start of construction to completion there was neither any petitioning about it nor violent confrontation. That is the borrower's statement; no independent record either way was found.
cases.outcome: An independent resettlement monitor hired for the project reported every six months and concluded that the affected people's livelihoods were better than before their land was acquired. Its sampling surveys showed average annual net income per head rising to RMB 3,200 after resettlement, an average increase of 7 per cent, with all sampled households earning more than before. The completion report states that the cash and in-kind compensation paid to the affected villages and persons was the same as or higher than the rates in the approved plan. The Independent Evaluation Group rated the project outcome Satisfactory and recorded that the risk of delay from the resettlement programme had been identified at appraisal but not adequately mitigated, with the result that construction was held up by more than six months, and that despite the delays the results were satisfactory according to the independent resettlement monitor.
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 25,393 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. No number given here matches it. The Bank's completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation give no total count of people displaced by the project. The only physical measures in the record are the borrower's figures for the Kunming Railway Administration section: 431,886 square metres of housing demolished and 5,587.4 mu of land newly acquired. Neither report separates people who lost housing from people who only lost land.

cases.title: Shiyan connecting road widened outside the plan, Hubei
cases.point: Approximate. Shiyan city, Hubei, where the 6 km connecting road was built. The expressway it connected to runs from Shiyan to Manchuanguan on the Shaanxi border; the completion report gives its length as 105.1 km in one place and 106.4 km in another.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Hubei Shiman Highway Project, P081749. Loan IBRD-47450 (L4745-CN) of US$200 million, approved 24 June 2004, effective 30 December 2004, with US$199.0 million disbursed and the revised amount recorded as US$199.0 million. The closing date was moved from 30 June 2009 to 31 December 2009. The completion report gives total project cost as US$533.90 million at appraisal against US$725.36 million actual, with the borrower's own financing rising from US$329.00 million estimated to US$527.00 million.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A. Resettlement was carried out under a Resettlement Action Plan, with a resettlement office set up by the Hubei Provincial Transportation Department and independent monitoring. The 6 km connecting road between the expressway and the city of Shiyan was part of the project as a class II road, with US$0.47 million of the loan allocated to it at a 20 per cent disbursement ratio.

companies.name: Hubei Provincial Transportation Department
companies.role: Implementing agency for the expressway and the local road improvement programme

companies.name: Shiyan Municipal Government
companies.role: Arranged the widening of the connecting road with the contractor and then financed the works itself

cases.community: The completion report states that the city of Shiyan arranged with the contractor of the original two-lane connecting road to widen it into a four- and six-lane road, that this was not in accordance with the Project Agreement, and that safeguards procedures were not followed. A Bank post-review mission in April 2006 found that Bank policies on procurement and safeguard were not strictly followed, and the connecting road was taken out of Bank financing; the works were paid for by the city of Shiyan. The report records that the change was made because the road lay in the Shiyan urban area and was required by the Shiyan municipal government, that the Bank was not informed of the change in advance, and that it was built together with Gansu Road, which the Bank did not finance. US$0.47 million of loan savings resulted and was reallocated in May 2007 to the expressway. The report's output table records the connecting road as completed under the project as a two-lane road, with the further widening to four and six lanes financed by Shiyan city. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation says how much land or housing the widened road took, or how many people lost either. For the project as a whole, carried out under the Resettlement Action Plan, 5,007 persons in 1,480 households were relocated and 60.6 thousand mu, about 4,020 hectares, of land were acquired. The completion report says those figures were lower than the plan had expected, after minor design adjustments to the expressway's alignment. That figure belongs to the resettlement carried out under the plan and not to the widened connecting road, for which no figure is given.
cases.outcome: The Independent Evaluation Group rated the project outcome Satisfactory and wrote that the project was written up as a case study jointly by the Bank and the University of Wuhan and in most respects was exemplary, except for the issue with the Shiyan road. The validation sets that issue out under fiduciary compliance and calls it the only issue in the project's procurement. A post-resettlement survey found that 75 per cent of affected families thought their livelihood had improved, 16 per cent that it had improved somewhat and 4 per cent that it had stayed the same; the report does not account for the remaining share. Houses in the resettlement sites were larger than those previously occupied and mostly of brick and concrete rather than earth and wood. The Independent Evaluation Group also recorded higher project costs than expected, caused in part by policy changes on resettlement compensation and by exceptionally heavy rains in 2007 that collapsed some slopes and retaining walls.
cases.displaced_label: persons in 1,480 households relocated under the project's Resettlement Action Plan (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 21,176 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. The Bank's completion report gives 5,007 persons in 1,480 households relocated and about 4,020 hectares of land acquired for the project as a whole, and says those figures were lower than the resettlement plan had expected. That count is for the resettlement carried out under the plan. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation gives any figure for land, housing or people for the widened connecting road in Shiyan, and neither separates people who lost housing from people who only lost land or income.

cases.title: Chebei Village replacement housing, Guangzhou
cases.place: Chebei, Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China
cases.point: Approximate. Chebei, in Tianhe District, Guangzhou, where 154 households were relocated for the project's wastewater works. The loan also paid for works in Foshan, Jiangmen and other Pearl River Delta municipalities.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Guangdong Pearl River Delta Urban Environment Project, P075728. Loan IBRD-47420 (L4742-CN) of US$128 million, approved 8 June 2004, effective 30 November 2004, with US$126.89 million disbursed. The closing date was moved from 31 December 2009 to 31 December 2011.

lenders.name: Global Environment Facility
lenders.role: Grant TF-53359 of US$10 million for the associated CN-GEF Guangdong PRD Urban Environment project, P084003, approved 8 June 2004 and closed 31 December 2011, with US$9.99 million disbursed.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A and involved involuntary resettlement for the land needed for wastewater treatment plants, sewer networks and a hazardous waste treatment facility. Resettlement Action Plans were prepared for the components. A restructuring took place on 5 February 2010.

companies.name: Guangzhou Sewerage Treatment Company (GSTC)
companies.role: Implementing unit for the Guangzhou wastewater component; the completion report holds it responsible for the pending resettlement issues at Chebei Village

companies.name: Guangdong World Bank Financed Projects Management Office
companies.role: Provincial project management office, placed under the Department of Finance

cases.community: The completion report states that resettlement was almost entirely completed by the end of 2011 except for the construction of replacement housing for Chebei Village, under the wastewater component. By 2009 a total of 154 households, 550 people, at the village had been relocated, but the replacement housing had not been completed when the loan closed on 31 December 2011. The report lists this under the heading Pending Issue, says the Guangzhou project management office was responsible for finishing the housing as soon as possible, and says the Bank would supervise the work through to satisfactory completion. The report also states that the Guangzhou Sewerage Treatment Company was responsible for the cases of improper fiduciary practices and the pending resettlement issues at Chebei Village, and that the slow construction progress caused by the resettlement problems could have been addressed had that company been more proactive in asking the municipal government to mediate with the affected people or in getting district agencies to realign the collection pipelines nearer the streams and canals to reduce the resettlement. On the Bank's own performance, the report says the team's safeguards experts followed up on the resettlement plan for Chebei Village in particular and supervised the area twice a year, but that given the seriousness of the land compensation and resettlement challenges in this project, the Bank could have devoted more supervision resources to working with the client on solving these issues. Across the whole wastewater component, 643 households and 6,780 people were relocated against a resettlement plan covering 6,030 households and 24,342 persons; 1,207 mu of land were acquired against 1,640 mu planned; and 238,868 square metres of housing were affected against 958,564 planned.
cases.outcome: In its comments printed in the completion report, the Borrower disputed the Bank's account. It stated that under Chinese Contract Law Guangdong and Guangzhou had fulfilled all the related duties and obligations of the Chebei Village resettlement issue and that the land acquisition had been completed, so there was no pending resettlement issue. It stated that "There is still serious dispute between two parties, and the assessment made by the Bank solely from the Bank's perspective in the ICR is not fair and Guangdong PMO requested to delete all the related Chebei Village resettlement issue from the ICR." The passages about Chebei Village remain in the report as published, and the request to delete them is printed beside them. The completion report rated the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group rated it Moderately Unsatisfactory and rated the risk to the development outcome Significant. The Independent Evaluation Group's validation does not name Chebei Village. It records that the completion report says resettlement had been completed by project closing except for replacement housing for one village affected by the wastewater component, that 154 households had been relocated and the housing had not been completed, that the Bank team reported to the Independent Evaluation Group that there had been a published announcement that Guangzhou had started construction of replacement housing for the affected households in 2013, and that "No information has been provided with respect to the location of the relocated households in the absence of uncompleted replacement housing." It adds that the Borrower disputes that any further action is required. The same validation records that the completion report says implementation of the Resettlement Action Plan was successful and that the livelihoods of project-affected persons had been fully restored.
cases.displaced_label: people in 643 households resettled by the closing date (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 48,289 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. The Bank's appraisal foresaw the project having to resettle nearly 45,000 people. The completion report's main text gives 6,780 people, in 643 households, resettled by the closing date. The Independent Evaluation Group's validation states that a figure of 17,562 persons resettled cited elsewhere in the completion report was an error. The Independent Evaluation Group attributes the fall from the appraisal estimate to more accurate surveys, a shorter sewer network, changes to the pipeline layout and the use of pipe-jacking, and records that the total cost of resettlement was nonetheless much higher than estimated because urban land prices in the area rose quickly. The reports do not separate people who lost housing from people who only lost land or income.

cases.confidence_note: Two sides are on the record and they do not agree. The World Bank's completion report says replacement housing for 154 households relocated from Chebei Village by 2009 was still unfinished when the loan closed at the end of 2011, and lists it under the heading Pending Issue. The Guangdong project management office, in comments printed in the same report, says all duties and obligations had been met and there was no pending issue, describes a serious dispute between the two parties, and asked for the passage to be removed. The Independent Evaluation Group records that no information was provided on where the relocated households were living while the replacement housing was unfinished. Beyond those accounts, no independent press report, NGO field study, court record or Inspection Panel complaint about the Chebei Village resettlement was found; searches in English and in Chinese returned only World Bank documents. The World Bank's own documents are the only source, so the facts of the harm rest on the lender reporting on its own project, and the borrower rejects them.

lvwhy.project: A World Bank loan and a Global Environment Facility grant paid for the wastewater works that required the land.
lvwhy.land: Land was taken in Chebei Village for the sewer network and the households were moved out before their replacement housing was built.

cases.point: Approximate. A point about halfway along the 360 km Jilin to Hunchun railway, which runs east from Jilin City through Jiaohe, Yanji and Tumen to Hunchun near the Russian and North Korean borders.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: JiTuHun Railway Project, P122321. Loan IBRD-80520 (L8052-CN) of US$200 million, approved 24 May 2011, effective 30 August 2011, closed 31 December 2016, with US$198.67 million disbursed. The project's total cost is recorded as about US$6.3 billion.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A and triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP 4.01), natural habitats (OP 4.04), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11), indigenous peoples (OP 4.10) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). A Resettlement Action Plan with grievance handling procedures and internal and external monitoring, and an Ethnic Minority Development Plan integrated with it, were written and published before approval. An indigenous peoples screening at appraisal found Korean minority villages in Jiaohe County and some Man minority villages in Yanji City inside the project area. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation gives any figure or outcome for those villages, so what happened to them is not on the record. The project's financial statements were audited each year by China's National Audit Office, and the 2014, 2015 and 2016 audit reports were published.

companies.name: Changji Railway Company
companies.role: Project company; carried out land acquisition and resettlement with local governments and hired the external monitoring team

cases.community: At appraisal the project expected to acquire about 17,000 mu, 1,133.3 hectares, permanently, of which 98 per cent was rural collective land, and to resettle 4,221 households, 24 per cent of them rural and 76 per cent urban. Buildings to be demolished were 39 per cent rural housing and 49 per cent urban housing, the rest residential, enterprise and school buildings, and the project was not expected to involve demolition of illegal structures. At project closure the completion report records 18,495 mu acquired, which the Independent Evaluation Group gives as 1,233 hectares against the 1,133.3 hectares estimated, and 5,508 households relocated against the 4,221 estimated at appraisal, with the appropriate compensation paid. The resettlement cost at project completion is estimated in the completion report at RMB 5.24 billion, 22 per cent higher than the approved project resettlement budget. The railway was fully opened to traffic in September 2015.
cases.outcome: The completion report states that the project complied with both social safeguard policies, that the company and local governments set up institutions to carry out resettlement, that affected villages and households were consulted on the alignment, station locations, compensation rates, relocation arrangements and livelihood restoration, and that an independent external resettlement monitoring and evaluation team worked for the whole of implementation and confirmed in its reports that the resettlement programme was carried out satisfactorily and in compliance with the project's safeguards documents. No finding of a failure in the resettlement, and no complaint, court case or protest connected with it, was found in the Bank's record or outside it. The completion report rated the project outcome Highly Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group rated it Satisfactory. The record shows a move of 5,508 households carried out and recorded as compliant, about 30 per cent more households than the appraisal estimate.
cases.displaced_label: households relocated at project closure (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 19,588 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014, a year before the line opened. The Bank's completion report gives 5,508 households relocated at closure against 4,221 estimated at appraisal, and 18,495 mu of land acquired against about 17,000 mu estimated. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation gives a number of people, and neither separates people who lost housing from people who only lost land or income.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: ShiZheng Railway Project, P099062. Loan IBRD-75570 (L7557-CN) of US$300 million, approved 24 June 2008, effective 18 November 2008, with US$297.06 million disbursed and the loan amount revised to US$297.06 million. The closing date was moved from 31 December 2013 to 30 November 2015. The project's total cost is recorded as about US$6.544 billion.

cases.conditions: The project was Environmental Category A and triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment (OP 4.01) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). A socio-economic assessment and a Resettlement Plan with household relocation and livelihood restoration schemes were prepared at appraisal, based on consultation with the households concerned. A restructuring took place on 21 August 2012.
cases.community: The socio-economic assessment at appraisal found that the project would require the acquisition of about 1,171.2 hectares of collective land on which 9,815 persons lived, the relocation of 3,029 households with 15,087 persons, and would otherwise affect 46 enterprises and nine schools with 4,134 persons. A further 886 hectares of collective land was to be used temporarily during construction, with compensation paid to the affected people and the land then returned to its owners. At project closure the implementing agency had acquired 10 square kilometres of land, 5.5 in Hebei and 4.5 in Henan, against the appraisal estimate of 11.5 square kilometres, and had paid the required compensation. A total of 4,752 households were relocated, 3,195 in Hebei and 1,557 in Henan, against the 3,029 households estimated at appraisal. House compensation averaged RMB 450 per square metre in Henan and RMB 600 to 800 per square metre in Hebei, which the completion report says is higher than the rates in the resettlement plan.
cases.outcome: The completion report states that the social safeguard policy was complied with, that the plan was prepared, reviewed and disclosed, that affected villages and households were consulted on the alignment, station locations, compensation rates, relocation arrangements and livelihood restoration, and that the external social monitoring carried out for the project concluded that the plan was implemented satisfactorily. No finding of a failure in the resettlement, and no complaint, court case or protest connected with it, was found in the Bank's record or outside it. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group both rated the project outcome Satisfactory. The record shows a move of 4,752 households carried out and recorded as compliant, 57 per cent more households than the appraisal estimate.
cases.displaced_label: households relocated at project closure (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: ICIJ estimates 150,873 people displaced by this project and places it in its confirmed-displacement table; the figure comes from the World Bank's own project documents and is current to 31 December 2014. No number given here matches it. The Bank's completion report gives 4,752 households relocated at closure against 3,029 households with 15,087 persons estimated at appraisal, and 10 square kilometres of land acquired against 11.5 estimated. The appraisal assessment separately counted 9,815 persons living on the land to be acquired and 4,134 persons at 46 enterprises and nine schools otherwise affected. Neither the completion report nor the Independent Evaluation Group's validation gives a number of people relocated at closure, and neither explains the gap with ICIJ's figure.

dropped.reason: Bucket (b), dropped on the owner's rule that a corridor project with no specific community and no documented failure is worse than a clean drop. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR2142, 2013, downloaded and read from disk) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2014). The project acquired 5,713 mu of permanent land including 3,040 mu of farmland and 2,459 mu of temporary land, relocated 698 households with 2,998 persons, affected 11 enterprises and spent RMB 262 million on resettlement; the external resettlement monitor's survey concluded that affected households restored their income and housing. ICIJ's 171,568 is more than fifty times the 2,998 persons the Bank's own documents record as relocated, and nothing in either document explains the difference. No failure, no named affected community, and no source outside the Bank's own documents.

dropped.candidate: Huai River Basin Flood Management and Drainage Improvement (P098078)
dropped.reason: Bucket (b), dropped. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR00004036, 2017) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2017). Design changes cut the number of people needing resettlement from 7,044 to 4,884 across Anhui, Jiangsu, Henan and Shandong; a resettlement action plan was prepared for each subproject; the completion report records full compliance with OP 4.12 and that the incomes and living conditions of all resettled people were at least maintained. ICIJ's 58,659 is close to the project's own target of 57,173 project-affected people whose incomes were to be improved, which the completion report reports as exceeded at 81,311 - that is a benefit indicator, not a count of people moved. Four provinces, no named affected community, no documented failure.

Bucket (c), nothing usable. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR3508, 2015, downloaded and read from disk) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2016). The completion report says only that the safeguard issues and compliance were well managed and gives no figure for land taken or households affected. The Independent Evaluation Group wrote that the completion report does not state compliance with each safeguard policy, that no information about mitigation activities, impacts and affected households is provided in order to validate compliance, and that the information had to be sought from the project team. So the record carries no figure for what was actually carried out. ICIJ's 45,578 therefore cannot be tested against anything, and there is no documented harm.

Bucket (b), dropped. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR2930, 2014) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2014). ICIJ's 31,547 is exactly the people figure in the original resettlement plan, which covered 4,994 households and 677 enterprises and shops in six cities. The completion report records that actual resettlement was scaled down because components were cancelled or adjusted, and that the final resettlement involved 2,467 households, 119 enterprises and shops and 6,080 people, with most activities completed in all project cities before the loan closed and resettlement rated satisfactory throughout. A separate finding of non-compliance in the 2007 external audit concerned the use of loan funds in Panjin and Fushun, not resettlement. No named affected community and no documented resettlement failure.

Bucket (b), dropped. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR3432, 2015), the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2016) and the Independent Evaluation Group's Project Performance Assessment Report (PPAR 127580, 2018). At closure the implementing agency had acquired 16 square kilometres of land against 17 estimated at appraisal and relocated 2,463 households against 2,029 estimated, with total compensation paid equivalent to the appraisal estimate and the external social monitoring concluding the plan was implemented satisfactorily. The 2018 Project Performance Assessment Report, whose mission interviewed the project's resettlement specialist, records that the right-of-way purchase affected farmers to varying extent, that the overall impact in a typical village was small, that affected households were relocated within their own villages with a mix of cash and land re-allocation and each signed a formal agreement with the local government, and that the resettlement plan was implemented satisfactorily. ICIJ's 25,784 is not matched by any figure in any of the three documents. No named affected community and no documented failure. This record is the same shape as the two railway cases kept from this batch, leads 3 and 26, and of the three it is the one the Bank's evaluators examined most closely; it is dropped only under the owner's rule that a corridor project with no specific community and no documented failure is a worse outcome than a clean drop. If the owner wants all three same-shape railway records on the map, this one belongs with them.

Bucket (b), dropped as too small to carry a case. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR1913, 2011) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2013). The completion report records that implementation of the resettlement plan finished in September 2009, that 37,541 mu (2,503 hectares) of land were acquired, that 57 households with 223 people were relocated, all within the same village and into new cement-brick houses, that 23 business enterprises were compensated, that farmers at the dam site who lost the most land were compensated above the plan rates, that 34 vulnerable people received a monthly pension of RMB 100 to 300, and that villages in the reservoir area lost less than five per cent of their land. ICIJ's 25,655 is not matched by any figure in either document. The documented physical displacement is 223 people and no failure is recorded.

Bucket (b), dropped. Opened: the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR1376, 2011) and the Independent Evaluation Group's validation (2013). In Guangxi the total land acquisition came to 864 hectares, 4.2 per cent above the resettlement plan, and 131 households with 559 persons were relocated against the 49 households and 151 persons estimated in the plan; the local government raised the land compensation rate at the dam site and RMB 236.7 million was paid out against a budget of RMB 66.0 million; the Independent Evaluation Group records average income per head at the dam site rising 112 per cent between 2003 and 2008 and 32 per cent in the reservoir area, and all relocated households building brick-concrete houses. In Guangdong the scale of land acquisition rose by 50 per cent from 56.6 hectares in the resettlement plan to 77.8 hectares. ICIJ's 16,805 is not matched by any figure in either document. 131 households relocated, no named affected community and no documented failure.
